nodes.description: HER kinetics on Pt(111) in acid (0.1 M HClO4) and alkaline (0.1 M NaOH) conditions
nodes.source_text: Table 1: Kinetic and thermodynamic parameters for Pt(111) surfaces in acid (0.1 m HClO4) and alkaline (0.1 m NaOH) conditions.[16a,b] Pt(111) acid: j0=0.21 mA cm-2, Tafel slope=-74 mVdec-1, ΔH0#=18 kJ mol-1, ΔHHupd=-42 kJ mol-1; alkaline: j0=0.01 mA cm-2, Tafel slope=-150 mVdec-1, ΔH0#=46 kJ mol-1, ΔHHupd=-41 kJ mol-1

nodes.description: HER polarization curves of polycrystalline Pt electrodes at different pH
nodes.source_text: Many experimental observations show that the HER activity is pH-dependent on a wide range of electrocatalysts, including single crystals, polycrystalline metals... The trend on these surfaces is identical: the activity gradually decreases with increased pH (Figure 1 a).
the Pt(111)–Mn(OH)₂ hybrid, with the strongest OH interaction, showed the worst HER activity

nodes.characterization_summary: Kinetic parameters for Pt(111): j0 = 0.21 mA cm-2 (acid), 0.01 mA cm-2 (alkaline); Tafel slope -74 mV dec-1 (acid), -150 mV dec-1 (alkaline); ΔH0# = 18 kJ mol-1 (acid), 46 kJ mol-1 (alkaline); ΔHHupd ≈ -42 kJ mol-1 independent of pH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/C nanoparticles show pH-dependent H_upd region with stronger hydrogen adsorption under alkaline conditions compared to acidic conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the shape of the H_upd region curves on Pt/C nanoparticles in acid and alkaline solutions are different, with a stronger hydrogen adsorption under alkaline conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance on Pt(111) increases with electrolyte pH, indicating slower hydrogen adsorption in alkaline media.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It was also found that the charge transfer resistance, which is inversely proportional to the rate of corresponding hydrogen adsorption, increased with the electrolyte pH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru(0001) possesses low water dissociation barrier but relatively strong hydrogen adsorption with negative ΔG_H*, prohibiting product desorption.
